criteria.ac: §5 scenario 1 — an allowed caller (uid on the governor's allow list) opens the Unix socket and sends an admit request; the governor reads the request and replies as it does today, and the accepted request's log line carries peer_uid.
criteria.verified: test/governor-peer-cred.test.mjs::"guard: an allowed uid proceeds and the accepted request's log line carries peer_uid", "allow-list source: served when the root-owned governor-config.json lists the uid", and the real kernel read "linux real-peer: a real kernel SO_PEERCRED read serves the caller's own uid and refuses others, mode-independent" — all passing (node --test, Linux CI).

criteria.ac: §5 scenario 2 — a caller whose uid is NOT on the allow list is replied { ok: false, reason: "caller-not-allowed" } without the request being read, and a connect log line is written with op "connect", refusal "caller-not-allowed", and the peer uid.
criteria.verified: test/governor-peer-cred.test.mjs::"guard: a disallowed uid is refused caller-not-allowed before the request is read" plus the refuse-others half of the "linux real-peer" real-kernel test — passing.

criteria.ac: §5 scenario 3 — the allow list is sourced solely from the root-owned governor-config.json (mode 0600) in the 0700 key dir: served when it lists the uid, every caller refused when it is missing or allow_uids is empty (fail closed), with no runner-influenceable input (argv/env/wire) able to authorize a caller.
criteria.verified: test/governor-peer-cred.test.mjs::"allow-list source: served when the root-owned governor-config.json lists the uid", "...a missing file yields an empty list and an empty list refuses every caller", "...a wrong file mode refuses to start (exit-2 class)", "...a non-array allow_uids is refused", "interpreter policy: TRUSTED_PYTHON_PATHS are absolute and outside any user-writable home", and "interpreter policy: a python3 shim on PATH is never executed" — all passing.

criteria.ac: §5 assertion — the TCP --listen listener applies no peer check and is unchanged by this ticket.
criteria.verified: Static/structural verification: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/governor.ts wires guardUnixConnection only onto the Unix listener (governorStart, the make((socket) => guardUnixConnection(...)).listen(socketPath, ...) call) while the optional TCP listener keeps the bare make((socket) => onConnection(state, socket)).listen(port, host, ...); no guard is attached to the TCP path. The full peer-cred suite passing confirms no regression to the Unix guard.
